questions.stem: A can finish a piece of work in 10 days and B can finish the same work in 15 days. In how many days will they finish the work if they work together?
questions.explanation: Let total work be LCM(10, 15) = 30 units. A's efficiency = 30/10 = 3 units/day. B's efficiency = 30/15 = 2 units/day. Combined efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day. Time taken together = 30 / 5 = 6 days.

questions.stem: A and B working together can complete a task in 12 days. If A alone can complete the task in 20 days, how many days will B take to complete the task alone?
questions.explanation: Let total work be LCM(12, 20) = 60 units. A+B efficiency = 60/12 = 5 units/day. A's efficiency = 60/20 = 3 units/day. Therefore, B's efficiency = 5 - 3 = 2 units/day. Time taken by B alone = 60 / 2 = 30 days.

questions.stem: A works exactly twice as fast as B. If both of them can together complete a piece of work in exactly 12 days, then A alone can complete it in:
questions.explanation: Let B's efficiency be 1 unit/day. Then A's efficiency is 2 units/day. Combined efficiency = 3 units/day. Total work = 12 days * 3 units/day = 36 units. Time for A alone = 36 / 2 = 18 days.

questions.stem: A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B in 20 days. They work together on it for 4 days. What fraction of the original work is physically left?
questions.explanation: Total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units. A's efficiency = 4. B's efficiency = 3. Combined = 7. Work done in 4 days = 7 * 4 = 28 units. Remaining work = 60 - 28 = 32 units. Fraction left = 32 / 60 = 8 / 15.

questions.stem: A is exactly 30% more efficient logically than B. How much exact time will they take strictly working together to complete a job which A alone formally could physically do in exactly 23 days?
questions.explanation: Let B's efficiency be 10. A is 30% more, so A's efficiency is 13. Total work = A's efficiency * A's time = 13 * 23 = 299 units. Working together, their combined efficiency is 13 + 10 = 23. Time taken together = 299 / 23 = 13 days.

questions.stem: A, B, and C can cleanly neatly do a piece of work in 20, 30, and 60 days respectively. In how many distinct formal days exactly can A do the work if he is physically assisted strongly by B and C exactly precisely on every third calendar day?
questions.explanation: Total work = LCM(20, 30, 60) = 60 units. Efficiencies: A=3, B=2, C=1. Cycle of 3 days: Day 1 (A only) = 3 units. Day 2 (A only) = 3 units. Day 3 (A+B+C) = 3+2+1 = 6 units. Total work in one 3-day cycle = 3 + 3 + 6 = 12 units. Number of cycles required = 60 / 12 = 5 cycles. Total days = 5 * 3 = 15 days.

questions.stem: A and B can safely formally do a piece of work precisely in 12 days, B and C identically in 15 days, C and A cleanly neatly in 20 days. If A, B, and C rigidly effectively efficiently work exactly entirely securely together, they precisely logically logically will definitely formally completely successfully finish the work strictly accurately exactly in:
questions.explanation: Total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units. (A+B)'s efficiency = 5. (B+C)'s efficiency = 4. (C+A)'s efficiency = 3. Summing these: 2(A+B+C) = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12. So, (A+B+C) combined efficiency = 12 / 2 = 6 units/day. Time taken together = 60 / 6 = 10 days.
